details: The unshifted bound $\mathrm{coVC}\le\mathrm E$ fails for one-concept classes on a nonempty stated domain: their coVC is one and their effective range is zero. The elementary corrected bound is $\mathrm{coVC}\le\max\{1,\mathrm E\}$; no new graph edge is asserted here.
proof: On the one-point domain take $\mathcal H=\{\{1\}\}$, the $n=1$ singleton class. Its absent zero labeling and present one labeling form a hollow one-star, so coVC is one. All concepts agree at every coordinate, so the effective range is zero. The old proof only works for hollow stars of size at least two: for each star coordinate, two distinct realized neighbours disagree there, so that coordinate belongs to the effective range. Separating the size-zero and size-one cases yields the corrected maximum bound.
name: Effective Range / co-VC Dimension
witness_verification: At $n=1$, the class contains one concept on one coordinate. The first parameter (effective range) is zero, and the second (coVC) is one. This is a strict endpoint counterexample only, not an unbounded-ratio or functional separation.
